review_note: Source-first independent review of pinned curves.tex L2536 using proof-masked source and Stage A semantic fields: A surjective morphism from a smooth k-curve to normal k-curve preserves geometrical regularity of the target through its function field and local normality under the stated domination; Stage A retains surjectivity and normality.
statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a surjective morphism
of curves over $k$. If $X$ is smooth over $k$ and
$Y$ is normal, then $Y$ is smooth over $k$.

statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

For a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth curves over $k$, the following are equivalent: the function-field extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable, the map of invertible differential sheaves $df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$ is generically nonzero, and $f$ is étale on a dense open subscheme of $X$. Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $X$ be a smooth proper
curve over $k$. Let $(\mathcal{L}, V)$ be a $\mathfrak g^r_d$ with $r \geq 1$.
Then one of the following two is true
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a $\mathfrak g^1_d$ whose corresponding morphism
$X \to \mathbf{P}^1_k$ (obtained from the two-dimensional subspace of sections as in the linear-series construction above)
is generically \'etale (equivalently its function field extension is finite separable), or
\item there exists a $\mathfrak g^r_{d'}$ on $X^{(p)}$ where
$d' \leq d/p$.
\end{enumerate}

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.

Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

\label{lemma-ramification-to-algebraic-closure}
Let $X$ be a smooth curve over a field $k$. Let
$\overline{x} \in X_{\overline{k}}$ be a closed
point with image $x \in X$. The ramification index of
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \subset \mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{k}}, \overline{x}}$
